findings.evidence: 3a. Levers, one each: (a) hook-led ..., (b) reply-led ..., (c) repost-led (a self-contained, quotable statement).
findings.fix: Cut the lever definitions to their non-obvious constraints only (contrast only when both sides are supported; the question must be one the author genuinely wants answered). The model already knows what a hook, a question and a quotable line are.

findings.evidence: 5. **Recommend one** and say why. First check the candidate against the objective ... If it fails, revise it or pick another variant.
findings.fix: Add a short 'before choosing, ask: what will this reader do in the first second?' heuristic for each objective, so the recommendation follows a decision framework rather than a pass/fail checklist.

findings.evidence: Add hashtag stacks, "link in bio", or unrelated @mentions or links. Keep a link only if it substantiates the claim, and prefer it outside the main post text.
findings.fix: Give a reason, as the other NEVER items do: for example, hashtag stacks and 'link in bio' read as spam and cost characters, and a link in the main text spends 23 weighted characters that the hook needs.

findings.evidence: 4c. Within 15 of the limit: trim further, or tell the user to confirm the count in X's composer.
findings.fix: Set a default with an escape hatch: 'Within 15 of the limit: trim until there are at least 15 characters to spare; only when trimming would drop a supplied fact or qualifier, keep it and tell the user to confirm the count in X's composer.'

findings.evidence: Over the limit and the essential content cannot fit: ask whether to make a thread; if you cannot ask, return three alternative threads
findings.fix: Resolve the branch where the user says yes to a thread. State whether VERSION 1-3 become three alternative threads or the three single-post variants stay and one THREAD is added (line 56). Name which output layout applies in each case so the 'yes' path matches the Output section.

findings.evidence: 3b. If the user supplies a finished draft and asks only to shorten it, make VERSION 1 a minimal-edit trim ... 3c. **Sensitive posts** ... replace (b) and (c) with quieter variants
findings.fix: Add one line for the overlap: when a sensitive draft is only to be shortened, VERSION 1 is the minimal-edit trim and VERSIONS 2-3 are quiet variants, and the objective stays clarity.
